events.title: Founding of St. Augustine, Florida
events.description: Spanish admiral Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded the settlement of St. Augustine on the northeastern coast of Florida.
events.significance: It is the oldest continuously inhabited European-established city in the contiguous United States and anchored Spanish control of Florida.

events.title: Michelangelo's David Unveiled
events.description: Michelangelo's marble statue of David was unveiled in Florence, Italy, after about three years of work.
events.significance: The statue became an iconic masterpiece of Renaissance sculpture and a symbol of the Florentine Republic.

events.title: Italy Announces Armistice with the Allies
events.description: The armistice between Italy and the Allied forces was publicly announced, following its secret signing on September 3, 1943. German forces then moved to occupy much of Italy.
events.significance: Italy's exit from the Axis marked a turning point in World War II in Europe and led to the Italian Campaign and the German occupation of northern and central Italy.

events.title: Treaty of San Francisco Signed
events.description: Japan and 48 Allied nations signed the Treaty of San Francisco, formally ending the state of war and Allied occupation of Japan.
events.significance: The treaty restored Japanese sovereignty and set the stage for Japan's postwar reintegration into the international community.

events.title: Ford Pardons Richard Nixon
events.description: U.S. President Gerald Ford granted a full and unconditional pardon to former President Richard Nixon for any crimes he may have committed while in office.
events.significance: The pardon was highly controversial, ended the prospect of Nixon's prosecution after Watergate, and is widely believed to have hurt Ford politically.
